headline: The American Football Foundation
threshold: By Lesson 10, you can greet your team, give numbers, times and yards, describe players and the field, ask simple questions, make polite requests and ask for help in Spanish, and start American Football Lesson 1.

lessons.title: Sounds and Greetings
lessons.objective: Say football words clearly and greet coaches, teammates and fans in Spanish.
lessons.focus: The five pure vowels, ch, j, ll, rr and the written accent; hello and goodbye

words.note: The written accent marks the stress: ba-LÓN.
Spanish vowels are short and pure: e-KEE-po.
J sounds like a strong English h. A woman is la jugadora.
A woman is la entrenadora.
The accent puts the stress on the first syllable: ÁR-bi-tro.
LL sounds like the y in yes: ro-DEE-ya.
RR is a strong trill; tap your tongue several times.
CH sounds like church. Chamarra is the Mexican word.
You will also hear la cancha.

words.en: Hi, my name is Sam and I'm a new player.
words.es: Hola, me llamo Sam y soy jugador nuevo.
words.note: A woman says jugadora nueva.
To a woman: compañera.
Informal, for teammates. To a coach or an older fan: ¿Cómo está usted?

words.en: How do you say "helmet" in Spanish?

lessons.speaking: Greet a teammate and your coach, say your name, and ask how to say one piece of gear in Spanish.

lessons.title: Numbers, Time and Measurements
lessons.objective: Give jersey numbers, practice times, scores, yards, weight and height in Spanish.
lessons.focus: Numbers 0 to 1,000, clock time, and yards, pounds, feet, inches and minutes

words.note: The plural is las yardas.
The plural is los pies. Used for height in the US.
A game has 4 quarters. Say el primer cuarto for the first quarter.
You can also say 6:30 as a las seis y media.

lessons.speaking: Tell a teammate your jersey number, your height and weight, and what time practice starts tomorrow.

lessons.title: Ser and Estar
lessons.objective: Describe players, the field and where people are using ser and estar.
lessons.focus: Ser for who or what someone is, estar for how they feel or where they are

words.note: A woman says cansada.
Use with estar: está lesionado.
A woman is la capitana.
Ser: who someone is.
Estar: a condition that can change.

words.es: La jugadora número 8 es muy rápida.

words.note: Use estar for where a person or thing is.

words.en: The game is at the stadium.
words.es: El partido es en el estadio.
words.note: An event takes ser for its location.

lessons.speaking: Tell a teammate how you feel today, what the field is like, and where the coach is.

lessons.title: Have, There Is, Need and Want
lessons.objective: Say what gear you have, need or want, and what everyone has to do at practice.
lessons.focus: Tener, hay, necesitar, querer and hay que + infinitive

words.note: In Mexico and the US, tacos are cleats.
Spanish uses tener for thirst: tengo sed.

words.en: Is there ice in the cooler?
You always have to wear your helmet.
words.es: Hay que usar el casco siempre.
words.note: Hay que + infinitive: what everyone must do.

words.en: Do you have a bandage for my ankle?
words.note: Tienes is informal, for a teammate.

lessons.speaking: Tell the equipment manager what gear you have, what you need, and ask if there is ice in the cooler.

lessons.title: Go, Do and Can
lessons.objective: Talk about where you go, what you do and plans for practice, the gym and game day.
lessons.focus: Ir, ir a + infinitive for plans, hacer and poder

words.note: In Mexican and US Spanish, a carne asada is a grill party, like a tailgate.

words.en: Can I go to the locker room?
We're going to do the warm-up.
words.note: Ir a + infinitive: a plan.

words.en: After practice, I lift weights in the gym.
words.es: Después de la práctica, hago pesas en el gimnasio.

words.en: Can you go get the ball?
words.note: Ir por means go get. Informal, between teammates.

words.en: Tomorrow we go to the stadium by bus.
words.es: Mañana vamos al estadio en autobús.

words.en: We're going to have a cookout in the parking lot.
words.es: Vamos a hacer carne asada en el estacionamiento.

lessons.speaking: Tell a teammate your plans for after practice and ask if they can go to the gym or the game with you.

lessons.title: Present Tense
lessons.objective: Say what you, your teammates and the coaches do every day at practice and games.
lessons.focus: Present tense of regular -ar, -er and -ir verbs for yo, tú, usted, nosotros and ellos

words.note: A woman is la aficionada.

words.en: I throw the ball and you catch it.
words.es: Yo lanzo el balón y tú lo atrapas.

words.note: Use the personal a before people as the object.

words.en: We practice on Mondays and Wednesdays.
words.es: Nosotros entrenamos los lunes y los miércoles.

words.en: The fans yell a lot at the stadium.
words.es: Los aficionados gritan mucho en el estadio.
El pateador practica todos los días.

lessons.speaking: Tell a new teammate what you and the team do at practice each week and what the coaches do.

lessons.title: Questions
lessons.objective: Ask who, what, where, when, how much and why at practice or at the stadium.
lessons.focus: Question words: qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, cuánto, cómo, por qué, cuál

words.note: For how many, use ¿cuántos? or ¿cuántas?
Two words mean why; porque, one word, means because.
Use ¿cuál es...? to ask for a name, number or position.

words.es: ¿Quién es el entrenador de la defensiva?

words.en: Why is there a flag on the field?
words.es: ¿Por qué hay un pañuelo en el campo?
words.note: Mexican broadcasters call the penalty flag el pañuelo.

lessons.speaking: Ask a fan or teammate at the stadium who the coach is, where your seat is, and when the game starts.

lessons.title: No, Never and How Much
lessons.objective: Say no, never, nobody, not yet, and ask for more, less or another at practice.
lessons.focus: No, nunca, nadie, nada, todavía no, más, menos and otro

words.note: Spanish uses a double negative: no veo nada.
Never put un before otro; say otro balón, otra toalla.

words.en: I never play without a helmet.
Nobody is in the locker room.
I can't see anything from here.

words.note: A woman says lista.

words.en: Today we run more and rest less.
words.es: Hoy corremos más y descansamos menos.

lessons.speaking: Tell a teammate you're not ready yet, that you never play without your helmet, and ask for another ball.

lessons.title: Polite Requests and Commands
lessons.objective: Politely ask a coach or staff member to repeat, pass or bring something.
lessons.focus: ¿Puede…? requests and usted commands for everyday verbs

words.en: Can you repeat the play, please?
words.note: ¿Puede...? is polite usted, good for a coach.

words.en: Can you pass me the whistle?

words.note: Usted command: hablar becomes hable.

words.en: Put the cones on the line, please.
words.es: Ponga los conos en la línea, por favor.

words.en: Open the locker room door, please.
words.es: Abra la puerta del vestidor, por favor.
Traiga el libro de jugadas, por favor.
words.note: To the whole team, a coach says traigan (ustedes).

lessons.speaking: Ask an assistant coach politely to repeat a play, speak more slowly, and bring you the cones.

lessons.title: Words You Already Know and Getting Help
lessons.objective: Spot football words you already know and ask for help when you don't understand.
lessons.focus: Cognates ending in -ción, -dad and -ente, plus survival phrases for getting help

words.note: -ción words are like English -tion and are feminine.
-dad words are like English -ty and are feminine.

words.en: Can you write it down for me, please?

words.note: Use the personal a before a person: al entrenador.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coach you speak a little Spanish, ask what a word means, and ask them to write it down for you.
